title: Bass one-shot synthesis parameters
description: Synthesis parameters for one deterministic, pitched, gated bass note (v0.1, proposal, #320). Mono. Only schema_version and seed are required; an omitted field takes the default named in its description. Out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped. Voice: up to three phase-0 sine-series oscillators (saw_level, square_level, sine_level) at the note frequency, an optional sine one octave below (sub_octave_level), a high-pass at hp_hz, a 2nd-order low-pass with an exponentially closing cutoff envelope (lp_hz, lp_q, lp_env_amount, lp_env_decay_ms), a linear attack ramp, a gate (gate_ms) and a linear release ramp (release_ms). The file length is gate_ms + release_ms (no length field). Time t is measured from the first sample of the sound (sample n_off with offset_ms). All numeric ranges and defaults are PROPOSALS from docs/research/2026-11-02_bass-targets.md section 2 and 5 and docs/research/2026-11-02_snare-rim-and-sub-bass-design.md section 3.3 (hypotheses; the only sourced numbers are from one Attack Magazine tutorial: high-pass about 65 Hz, low-pass about 350 Hz, note G2 = 98 Hz = MIDI 43; nothing is sourced for levels, times, resonance, envelope depth or drive); they are placeholders until the audio-engineer measures them and the user listens. The audio-engineer may adjust them in the engine PR (a contract-change then). Not part of v0.1: detune / reese (`detune_cents`), a `model` field (FM rumble), stereo, a bass line or pattern, sidechain, new sidecar features (harmonic ratios, sub share etc. are design and test helpers first).
$comment: Contract rules that JSON Schema cannot express or that are not field ranges. (1) Note frequency: f0 = 440 * 2^((note - 69) / 12) * 2^(cents / 1200) Hz (note 43 = 98.0 Hz, note 24 = 32.7 Hz, note 55 = 196.0 Hz). The note name is printed together with the Hz in every response (kick genre-words note). Key / note-name resolution is not part of this contract. (2) Cross-field rules, checked by the engine with an error text (never clamped; the schema cannot compare fields): (a) hp_hz must be less than 0.8 * f0, with the default hp_hz (20) satisfied for every note in range (0.8 * 32.7 = 26.2); an explicit hp_hz of 40 breaks it for notes below about 50 Hz (note 31: limit 39.2 Hz), B1's 65 Hz needs a note of 82 Hz or more; (b) lp_hz must be at least 1.2 * hp_hz; (c) lp_hz * 2^lp_env_amount (the cutoff at t = 0) must be less than 0.45 * sample_rate; (d) at least one of saw_level, square_level, sine_level, sub_octave_level must be greater than 0 (otherwise silence). amp_attack_ms (at most 30) is always shorter than gate_ms (at least 50), so no rule is needed for that pair. (3) Oscillators: every oscillator is a sine series with phase 0 at t = 0: sine = sin(2 pi f0 t); saw = sum over k of sin(2 pi k f0 t) / k; square = sum over odd k of sin(2 pi k f0 t) / k; sub = sin(2 pi (f0 / 2) t). Partials are exact (additive), limited to k * f0 below 0.45 * sample_rate. The level of each oscillator is the amplitude of its first partial (k = 1; for sub, its only partial); the sum is then normalised to peak_ceiling_dbfs, so only ratios matter. (4) Filter semantics (decision 5 of the bass note): lp_hz is the sustained cutoff, the cutoff at the end of the envelope. The cutoff at time t is lp_hz * 2^(lp_env_amount * 10^(-3 * t / lp_env_decay_ms)), so it starts lp_env_amount octaves above lp_hz and the excess (in octaves) has fallen to 0.1 % after lp_env_decay_ms (the same 'time to -60 dB' idea as kick amp_decay_ms). lp_env_amount 0 means a fixed cutoff. hp_hz is a fixed 2nd-order high-pass. (5) Amplitude: a linear ramp from 0 to 1 over amp_attack_ms starting at the first sample; hold until gate_ms; then a linear ramp from the held level to 0 over release_ms. The first sample and the last sample are 0. File length = gate_ms + release_ms plus offset_ms, rounded to whole samples; length_ms is derived and is not an input. (6) Pitch in the sidecar: fundamental_hz is the engine's note frequency f0 as measured in the stationary window, not f0 / 2 when sub_octave_level > 0 (decision 6). The stationary window is 40 % to 80 % of gate_ms (counted from the end of offset_ms). If that window holds fewer than 2 whole periods of f0 (for example note 24 with gate_ms below about 153 ms) fundamental_hz is null; it is never taken from the release. The kick tail_window is not used for bass. (7) Determinism: oscillators, filters and ramps have no randomness. seed is kept for sidecar uniformity and for variants; at v0.1 the core voice is seed-independent, and variants jitter other fields inside a preset box (decision 8). Same parameters and seed give a byte-identical WAV. (8) Measurement method per field (decision: pitch tooling that assumes a decaying one-shot is unusable for bass; analyse() tail_window lands in the release, rise_time_ms and t60_ms read a 1 ms RMS envelope that ripples by 9 to 34 dB on sustained notes, bass note section 3 P1/P2). Fields are verified on single renders with the other stages neutral (drive 0, lp_env_amount 0 unless it is the field under test): note and cents by two independent methods in the stationary window, zero-crossing frequency and a long-window spectral peak with interpolation (or autocorrelation), compared over the same interval, in cents; saw_level, square_level, sine_level, sub_octave_level by the level of the partials at k * f0 (and f0 / 2) in the stationary window, rectangular window over a whole number of periods, at least 8 periods of the analysed frequency, relative to the first partial; hp_hz, lp_hz and lp_q by the level of the partials of a saw render (lp_env_amount 0) against the 2nd-order filter response written in the test (not read from the engine), lp_q by the partial nearest lp_hz; lp_env_amount and lp_env_decay_ms by the ratio of the spectral centroid in the first 30 ms to that in the stationary window, only valid for notes where 30 ms holds at least 1 period (about 60 Hz and above, note 35 and up); a longer gate is used to see the decay; amp_attack_ms on a peak envelope (maximum of |x| per half period) as the time from the first sample to 90 % of the stationary peak, with a tolerance of one period of f0 (one period at note 24 is 30.6 ms, longer than the attack range, so the attack is read at notes of 35 and above, or with the envelope of a sine-only render); gate_ms and release_ms from the quantised file: file length is exact, release as the time from gate end until the last sample with |x| >= 0.01 (-40 dB) of the stationary peak (the stationary peak is the maximum of |x| in the stationary window); it lies at most one period of f0 before 0.99 * release_ms, where 0.99 * release_ms is the time at which the linear ramp itself reaches 0.01; no upper bound is claimed (measured on engine renders with drive 0 and lp_env_amount 0, notes 24 to 55, releases 5 to 400 ms: from -0.03 to -2.98 ms, never above, cause of the exact offset not established); read only where release_ms is at least 4 periods of f0 (note 24 needs about 122 ms; shorter releases are not read); a period-long RMS envelope (window = max(5 ms, one period of f0)) is not used for the release because the linear ramp ends at 0 with the file and the window still holds it, so -40 dB is never reached for default-like releases; start and end click as the largest sample-to-sample step in the first and last 5 ms against the stationary peak; drive by harmonics at 2 * f0 and 3 * f0 and by alias energy against a render at 4 times the sample rate; DC as the mean of the file. rise_time_ms and t60_ms are not used for bass. (9) No taste range: no published numeric target exists for sub share, harmonic ratios or centroid of a techno/trance bass; analysis reports, it does not pass or fail on those. (10) Reject out-of-range values, never clamp. Defaults are placeholders until measured. The default note is 43 (98.0 Hz, the only sourced value); the researcher default 31 (49.0 Hz) lies inside the user's 45-60 Hz kick tails, both are hypotheses (decision 1). Shared field names keep the meaning of clap-params and kick-params (seed, variants, bpm, sample_rate, bit_depth, drive, polarity, offset_ms, peak_ceiling_dbfs, preset). Engine identity for sidecars: engine.name 'abeltongod-audio-engine-bass' with the bass engine's own version (sample-metadata.schema.json, D-025).

seed.description: Kept for sidecar uniformity and variants. The core voice is seed-independent at v0.1. Same parameters and seed give a byte-identical WAV.

note.description: MIDI note number of the fundamental, 24 (32.7 Hz) to 55 (196.0 Hz). Default 43 = G2 = 98.0 Hz (the only sourced value).

saw_level.description: Amplitude of the first partial of the saw series.

square_level.description: Amplitude of the first partial of the square (odd partials) series.

sine_level.description: Amplitude of the sine at the note frequency.

sub_octave_level.description: Amplitude of a sine one octave below the note. 0 = off. Does not change the meaning of fundamental_hz (the note, not the octave below).

gate_ms.description: Time the note is held at full level, from the first sample (attack included).

release_ms.description: Linear release ramp to 0 after the gate. File length is gate_ms + release_ms.

amp_attack_ms.description: Linear attack ramp from 0 to full level, ms.

hp_hz.description: Corner of the 2nd-order high-pass, Hz. Must be less than 0.8 * the note frequency (cross-field rule, checked by the engine). The default 20 satisfies it for every note.

lp_hz.description: Sustained cutoff of the 2nd-order low-pass, Hz (the cutoff at the end of the envelope). At least 1.2 * hp_hz, and lp_hz * 2^lp_env_amount below 0.45 * sample_rate (engine rules).

lp_env_amount.description: Octaves the cutoff starts above lp_hz at t = 0. 0 = fixed cutoff.

lp_env_decay_ms.description: Time for the excess cutoff (in octaves) to fall to 0.1 % (exponential). No effect at lp_env_amount 0.

drive.description: Anti-aliased saturation, same stage as kick drive. 0 = off.

polarity.description: Sign of the whole output, applied after the peak ceiling.

offset_ms.description: Silence before the sound, rounded to whole samples (as in kick-params).

peak_ceiling_dbfs.description: Peak ceiling of the quantised file.

preset.description: Name of the preset these values came from, if any.
